_comment: DECLARATIVE default 4-desktop login layout — single source of truth. Captured live from the running KWin/Konsole session on 2026-06-18 (screen 2304x1536, panel 44px → usable 1492px; every split is at the exact half x=1152). Consumed by default-session.nix → default-session-launcher.sh (the engine) + generated Konsole --tabs-from-file files + kwinrulesrc. Edit THIS file to change the layout, never the launcher. Geometry is stored as logical cells (left|right|full); the launcher computes pixels from the LIVE screen geometry at runtime so the layout is resolution-independent and reproducible on any machine.

screen_reference._work_area_doc: KWin MaximizeArea, measured live 2026-08-21 (panels excluded). NOTE this is 1426 tall, not the 1492 the older usable_height claimed - that value predates the current panel setup. Re-measure with a KWin script calling workspace.clientArea(KWin.MaximizeArea, w).

_virtual_desktops_doc: THE source of truth for how many virtual desktops exist. Two consumers,
one datum, so they cannot drift:
— the declarative path, applied at switch time via kwinrc.
the launcher verifies the live count over KWin's DBus VirtualDesktopManager
and creates any that are missing — the runtime safety net.
Both are needed. kwinrc is exactly the kind of file KWin rewrites from its
own in-memory state, which is how the systray lists were lost; a declaration
that is only ever written at switch time can be silently undone before the
next one. And the layout below targets desk5 — placing a window on a desktop
that does not exist puts it wherever KWin feels like, which reads as 'the
layout is broken' rather than 'a desktop is missing'.
count MUST cover the highest id used in .desktops[] below.

fallback._comment: Guarantees a crashing/hanging app can NEVER hold the login. The launcher runs from a Plasma autostart entry with X-KDE-autostart-condition=ksmserver and phase=2 — i.e. AFTER the session is up, so it cannot block login. (It is NOT a systemd oneshot; this line said so until 2026-08-21.) Each app is spawned detached, and each launch is wrapped in `timeout`. A failed/timed-out launch is logged (and ntfy'd) and the launcher moves on to the next app.
fallback._gate_doc: There is deliberately NO boot-type knob here any more. run_on/fresh_only tested `noresume` on /proc/cmdline: a per-BOOT signal answering a per-SESSION question, and it tested which rEFInd entry was booted rather than what the kernel actually did. On 2026-08-21 cmdline carried resume= while the kernel loaded ZERO hibernation images - a genuinely fresh session that got no layout. A real resume restores the session from the RAM image, so ksmserver never restarts and this launcher never runs; the gate could only ever be a false negative. The guard is now emptiness: the launcher skips if any of the layout apps are already running.
fallback._position_doc: Positioning re-asserts (desktop + tile) idempotently across several passes so SLOW-to-map windows (e.g. systemsettings under dbus-run-session, electron apps) still get placed. passes × interval should exceed the slowest window's map time.

_apps_doc: App registry — the launcher is GENERIC and reads everything here. To add/change an app you edit ONLY this block + reference it from a desktop window by its key. type=konsole gets the tab/title builder (matched for positioning by PID). For every other app: exec=binary, match_class=KWin resourceClass used to find its window for positioning (case-insensitive), fixed_args=always-passed args, arg_mode=how the window's per-instance value is appended: path→args[0], url→url (single), urls→urls[] (one browser tab per URL), paths→args[] (existing dirs only), none→nothing. single_instance=true means a second launch would fold into the ALREADY RUNNING process instead of creating a window this launcher can match by PID - skip it. Default false: konsole is launched --separate --nofork precisely so desk3 can hold two windows while desk1 has one.

kate._single_instance_doc: Kate reuses its running instance by default (Behavior > Open each document in its own window is off), so a second launch adds a document to the existing window rather than a new one to position.

cloud-terminal._doc: Cloud Terminal (Electron, da_cloud-terminal). Launcher on PATH via `build.sh install` → ~/.local/bin. --class sets the Wayland app_id = resourceClass used for positioning.

redroid._doc: Redroid Android (da_redroid). The `redroid` launcher (HM containers-cloud/redroid.nix, ~/.local/bin) runs `redroid up` = docker pull+run the BAKED redroid-cloud GHCR image (apps + layout + theme baked in), then scrcpy to mirror it. match_class=scrcpy is the mirror window's Wayland app_id used for positioning. NOTE: first-ever login after a fresh pull may exceed the per-app launch timeout while the multi-GB image downloads — fallback logs+continues (never blocks login); the window lands on Desktop 3 on subsequent logins once the image is cached.

brave._single_instance_doc: Brave is one process: a second `brave` invocation opens a tab/window inside the running one and exits, so the launcher can never match the new window by PID. Skip instead of guessing.

windows._comment: 5 tabs: yazi, fzf, home (plain), ___ (plain), my-ai. command runs in the tab-s root pane; missing binary falls back to a plain shell.
Left half only. The right half is deliberately empty - kate is the whole point of this desktop and a second window would just be in the way.
Live journal views. The -f tabs follow; boot and errors are one-shot snapshots of the current boot.
Deliberately empty - a plain shell to work in, under the journals. No command, so it is just fish.

ONE window, full height, split top/bottom: atop above, htop below. dir=tb splits the pane horizontally into a top and a bottom half; pane=0 targets the tab root, so the new pane is the bottom one and takes htop while the root keeps atop.
arg_mode=paths - dolphin opens ONE TAB PER PATH, so this list is the tab bar left to right. Details view is the default via dolphinrc GlobalViewProps (see plasma.nix).

_konsole_cell_doc: Konsole sizes itself in CHARACTER CELLS. On Wayland the CLIENT decides its size - KWin sends a configure and Konsole answers with the nearest whole cell count - so the -p TerminalColumns/TerminalRows values at launch ARE the final geometry. Nothing compositor-side overrides them: not frameGeometry, not quick-tile, not the strictgeometry window rule (an X11-era hint, tested with no effect).
Measured 2026-08-21 from three live windows: 39 rows -> 655px, 40 -> 671, 84 -> 1375.
and across the width: 160 cols -> 1152px, so cell_w = 7, pad_w = 1152 - 160*7 = 32.

An earlier derivation from two THROWAWAY konsoles gave pad_h=77, and that 46px error is what left a seam between the stacked windows. Measure the windows the layout actually creates, not test ones - the frame differs.
A stacked pair must be sized AS A PAIR: total = (h - 2*pad)/cell, top = ceil(total/2), bottom = the rest. Independent halves do not meet.
